market: Spain (BME Mercado Continuo and BME Growth / BME Scaleup)
fx: All figures in EUR (local currency); no conversion needed. EV band EUR 130m-650m at EUR/USD 1.15 per 00_brief.md.
universe_scanned: stockanalysis.com/list/madrid-stock-exchange/ (290 names, all BME-traded equities incl. BME Growth and BME Scaleup, scanned in full on 4 Nov 2026; roughly half are SOCIMIs, foreign Latibex lines or industrials). The BME Growth official list page (bolsasymercados.es/es/bme-growth/.../empresas-cotizadas.html) loads dynamically and returned no names. Sector pages on stockanalysis do not exist for BME, so the full list was read name by name.
verdict: Spain's pool is thin. Of 290 lines, only four are on-vertical and inside or near the EV band with a plausible path to control or real influence: Alantra (wealth/asset management plus advisory, founder-pact block), Indexa Capital (robo-adviser, founder block, moving to Mercado Continuo), Atrys Health (healthcare services, 27.7% strategic holder, post-restructuring) and Renta 4 (wealth platform, but it is a licensed bank with a 40% founder). Everything else is either an IT-services house with a 55-99% owner (Izertis, Altia, ATSI), too small (Facephi, Seresco, Lleida.net, Making Science, Axon), too large or strategically locked (Clinica Baviera, Prosegur Cash, Linea Directa), or off-vertical (Dominion). No listed Spanish insurance broker, payments company, HR/finance software vendor or compliance software vendor of band size exists; the closest are sub-EUR 50m BME Growth names that only work as add-ons (Facephi for IDnow, Seresco for an HR-software platform).
gone_since_2024: Applus Services (testing/inspection; adjacent to professional services): contested bids by Apollo and Amber (I Squared/TDR); Amber won at EUR 12.78/share, 70.65% in the initial offer, delisting offer at the same price approved by the board June 2024; delisted H2 2024.
Opdenergy (renewables, off-vertical): Antin/GCE Bidco EUR 5.85/share, acceptance 22 Feb-15 Mar 2024, 99.6% acceptance, squeeze-out and delisting 2024.
Tier1 Technology (BME Growth retail software): Retex S.p.A. (Italy) EUR 3.00/share cash, 12.8% premium, 71.92% acceptance, settled 27 Dec 2024, delisted 14 Feb 2025.

Grupo Catalana Occidente (insurer): Inocsa (Serra family) EUR 50/share March 2025 (adjusted to EUR 49.2 then EUR 45.10 for dividends), squeeze-out, delisted (late 2025/early 2026 per forum sources; CNMV register 427).

Agile Content (BME Growth, video/CDN software): shareholder-approved delisting 25 June 2026 with an associated purchase offer; BME excluded the 23.2m shares from trading effective 3 Aug 2026 at the company's own request.
jurisdiction_rules: RD 1066/2007 (consulted at boe.es): mandatory bid at 30% of voting rights (art. 4); delisting requires a cash exclusion offer approved by the AGM at a price not below the 'equitable price' and an independent valuation (arts. 9-10); exemptions where squeeze-out conditions are met (art. 11). Squeeze-out/sell-out (art. 47, not reached in the truncated fetch but well established): offeror must hold 90% of voting capital and the bid must have been accepted by 90% of the shares it was addressed to, exercisable within three months. BME Growth issuers delist via AGM resolution plus a purchase offer (Circular rules), as Tier1 and Agile Content did.
